registryBasis: City-specific evidence is a 2019 Freetown City Council property geo-mapping campaign for a tax database; it collected compound GPS/attributes and did not describe cadastral parcel boundaries. Sierra Leone’s land-administration project includes planned registration work in Freetown, while the NLC public digital portal remains in pilot/development. These do not establish a current city-wide parcel register, so registryFound is null.
findings: Freetown City Council documents a city-wide property geocoding campaign for taxation, collecting GPS and compound attributes rather than parcel-boundary polygons. The World Bank land-administration project describes cadastral-index and registration work planned for Freetown; the NLC portal is still in development/pilot. These sources show land-data activity but do not establish a currently accessible, complete city parcel register. No public parcel feature service was verified.
